title: Sell Mineral Rights in Pinson, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Pinson, AL | Jefferson County
metaDescription: Own mineral rights tied to older Pinson, AL family farmland? We check the Jefferson County title before making a fair, no-pressure offer.
heroLead: Pinson has grown into a Birmingham suburb over the last few decades, but a good share of the land underneath the newer subdivisions was farmland held by the same families for generations, and the mineral rights often stayed with the original owners even after the surface was developed or sold.
intro: As Pinson has grown, a lot of older farm tracts have been subdivided, sold to developers, or simply passed down while the surrounding area filled in with houses. What frequently gets overlooked in that process is the mineral estate — a family may have sold the surface for development while quietly keeping the minerals, or the mineral rights may never have transferred at all when a parcel changed hands informally within the family. Either way, the mineral interest can remain fully intact long after the ground above it looks nothing like it did a generation ago.

sections.heading: When the Surface Sold But the Minerals Didn't
paragraphs: If your family sold land near Pinson for a subdivision or commercial development, it's worth checking whether the mineral rights were actually included in that sale or reserved. A lot of older deeds in this area are silent or ambiguous on the point, and we read them carefully before telling you what your family still holds.

sections.heading: What Growth Has and Hasn't Changed
paragraphs: Pinson's growth as a community hasn't changed what's under the ground — the same coalbed methane trend that runs through north Jefferson County still applies here. We check whether your family's mineral interest sits inside an active unit, and if it does, we price against the actual royalty history rather than guessing based on how built-up the surface has become.

faqs.question: We sold our land for a subdivision years ago. Could we still own the minerals?
faqs.answer: Possibly — many older deeds don't clearly convey mineral rights along with the surface. We read your specific deed to find out.

faqs.question: Does it matter that houses have been built on top of the old farm?
faqs.answer: Not for mineral ownership. Surface development doesn't affect who owns what's below it, though it can affect how a well is sited if the tract were ever drilled directly.

faqs.question: How do we find out if our interest is in a producing unit?
faqs.answer: Send us the legal description from an old deed or probate file, and we'll check it against current state pooling records.
